chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Junah, from Awf ibn Abd Allah al-Azdi, from his paternal uncle, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about capability, so he said: 'Have they done so?' I said: 'Yes. They claim that it does not exist except at the time of the action and an intention during the time of the action, not before it.' He said: 'The people have disbelieved.'

key_terms.أشرك القوم: The people have disbelieved/associated partners (used here as a strong theological verdict)
key_terms.الاستطاعة: Capability or ability to perform an action
key_terms.وقد فعلوا: Have they done so? (Rhetorical question indicating surprise or confirmation)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about the timing of human capability and intention?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* addresses the Mu'tazili and Shia debate on whether 'istita'ah' (capability) is a pre-existing attribute or an event concurrent with the act. The Imam (AS) critiques the view that capability arises only at the moment of action, labeling it as a form of *shirk* (associating partners with God) because it implies that God's power is limited to the instant of execution rather than being an eternal, encompassing attribute. This highlights the Shia theological stance that human capability is a created attribute granted by God, distinct from His eternal power.
